Appendix B • Proofs & Comments

B.15 Higher-order Lagrangians (§7.2.1)

The Lagrangian of Chapter 7 is a function on the tangent bundle: it eats a tangent vector \(\mathcal{X}_p\), i.e. a base point and a velocity, and nothing else. Its chart representative therefore has only position slots and velocity slots, and the action of a curve only involves \(\gamma_\mathcal{U}\) and \(\dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}\). Higher derivatives appear as soon as the integrand also depends on the acceleration of the curve, or on even higher derivatives. This happens, for instance,

  • for Lagrangians built from the acceleration \(a_\gamma = \nabla_{v_\gamma} v_\gamma\) of Chapter 6, whose components \(\ddot{\gamma}^k_\mathcal{U} + \Gamma^k_{ji} \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U} \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}\) contain second derivatives of \(\gamma_\mathcal{U}\);

  • when a total derivative is added to a first-order Lagrangian (item 3 of the remarks below);

  • in field theory, where the Lagrangian of General Relativity contains second derivatives of the metric components.

This appendix extends Appendix B.14 to Lagrangians depending on derivatives of \(\gamma_\mathcal{U}\) up to an arbitrary order \(k \geq 1\), following Section 2.1 of Ortín (2004), there written for fields. The case \(k = 1\) is the one of that appendix, and the proof follows the same five steps; only step 4 changes, since each order of derivative needs its own integrations by parts.

Setting. Let \((\mathcal{U}, \mathscr{X})\) be a chart, \(\gamma\) a smooth curve with \(\gamma([a,b]) \subseteq \mathcal{U}\), and \(\gamma_\mathcal{U} = \mathscr{X} \circ \gamma\). For \(j = 0, 1, \dots, k\) write \[ \gamma^{(j)}_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \coloneqq \frac{d^j}{d\lambda^j} \gamma_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \in \mathbb{R}^d, \qquad \gamma^{(0)}_\mathcal{U} = \gamma_\mathcal{U}, \quad \gamma^{(1)}_\mathcal{U} = \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}, \] where the index in parentheses counts derivatives (it is not a slot label as in Chapter 2). A Lagrangian of order \(k\) is, in the chart, a smooth function \[ \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X} : D_\mathscr{X} \subseteq \underbrace{\mathbb{R}^d \times \dots \times \mathbb{R}^d}_{(k+1) \text{-times}} \longrightarrow \mathbb{R}, \qquad \big( \alpha_{(0)} \, ; \alpha_{(1)} \, ; \dots ; \alpha_{(k)} \big) \longmapsto \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}\big( \alpha_{(0)} \, ; \alpha_{(1)} \, ; \dots ; \alpha_{(k)} \big), \] on an open set \(D_\mathscr{X}\) containing the points \(\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k)}_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \big)\), \(\lambda \in [a,b]\). Its \((k+1) d\) slots come in \(k+1\) blocks of \(d\) slots: block \(j\) receives the \(j\)-th derivative of the curve. Generalizing \(\partial_m\) (block \(0\)) and \(\partial_{d+m}\) (block \(1\)), \[ \partial_{jd+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X} \coloneqq \text{derivative of } \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X} \text{ w.r.t.\ the } m\text{-th slot of block } j . \] The action of \(\gamma\) is \[ S_{[a,b]}[\gamma] \coloneqq \int_a^b \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k)}_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \big) \, d\lambda , \] and the length of Chapter 7 is the case \(k = 1\), \(\mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X} = \sqrt{ \textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma \, g_{ij}\big( \mathscr{X}^{-1}(\alpha_{(0)}) \big) \, \alpha^i_{(1)} \alpha^j_{(1)} }\). Variations are defined as before, \(\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ}} = \gamma_\mathcal{U} + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}\), so that the \(j\)-th derivative of the varied curve is \(\gamma^{(j)}_\mathcal{U} + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(j)}\); but now we require \[ \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(i)}(a) = \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(i)}(b) = 0, \qquad i = 0, 1, \dots, k-1 : \] the varied curves share with \(\gamma\) not only the endpoints, but also the first \(k - 1\) derivatives of the chart representative there. The curve \(\gamma\) is a critical curve of the action if \(\frac{d}{d\textrm{\runic ᛊ}} S_{[a,b]}[\gamma_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ}}] \big|_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ} = 0} = 0\) for every such \(\textrm{\runic ᛉ}\).

Remark (charts). For \(k \geq 2\) the slots beyond the velocity are not the components of tangent vectors: under a change of chart, \(\ddot{\gamma}_\mathcal{V}\) is not obtained from \(\ddot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}\) with one Jacobian, but picks up second derivatives of the chart transition map, exactly as the connection coefficient functions do (Chapter 6). Hence a Lagrangian of order \(k \geq 2\) is not a function on \(T\mathcal{M}\); its natural home is a higher-order generalization of the tangent bundle, which these notes do not need. Everything below is done in a single chart.

Statement. \(\gamma\) is a critical curve if and only if, for \(m = 1, \dots, d\) and all \(\lambda \in [a,b]\), \[ \boxed{ \sum_{j=0}^{k} (-1)^j \frac{d^j}{d\lambda^j} \Big[ (\partial_{jd+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} \, ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} \, ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k)}_\mathcal{U} \big) \Big] = 0 . } \] For \(k = 1\) the left-hand side is \((\partial_m \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})(\gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}) - \frac{d}{d\lambda} \big[ (\partial_{d+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})(\gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}) \big]\), the bracket of step 4 of Appendix B.14: minus the left-hand side of its Statement.

Proof.

  1. 1–2.

    Admissibility, and differentiation under the integral sign. As in Appendix B.14, with the compact set \(K \subseteq D_\mathscr{X} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{(k+1)d}\) and the bound \(M_\textrm{\runic ᛉ}\) now including all blocks: \[ K \coloneqq \Big\{ \big( \gamma_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k)}_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \big) \;\Big|\; \lambda \in [a,b] \Big\}, \qquad M_\textrm{\runic ᛉ}^2 \coloneqq \max_{\lambda \in [a,b]} \sum_{j=0}^{k} \sum_{m=1}^d \big( \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(j)m}(\lambda) \big)^2 . \]

  2. Chain rule. At fixed \(\lambda\) (dropped from the notation), \(\textrm{\runic ᛊ}\) enters all \((k+1)d\) slots of \(\mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}\), block \(j\) through \(\gamma^{(j)}_\mathcal{U} + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(j)}\): \begin{align*} &\frac{\partial}{\partial \textrm{\runic ᛊ}} \Big[ \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ} \, ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k)}_\mathcal{U} + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(k)} \big) \Big] \Big|_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ} = 0} \\ \xlongrightarrow{\text{chain rule}} \; &\sum_{j=0}^{k} \sum_{m=1}^d \frac{\partial \big( \gamma^{(j)m}_\mathcal{U} + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(j)m} \big)}{\partial \textrm{\runic ᛊ}} \, (\partial_{jd+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ} \, ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k)}_\mathcal{U} + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(k)} \big) \Big|_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ} = 0} \\ \xlongrightarrow{\text{affine in } \textrm{\runic ᛊ}, \; \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, = \, 0} \; &\sum_{j=0}^{k} \sum_{m=1}^d (\partial_{jd+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} \, ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k)}_\mathcal{U} \big) \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(j)m} . \end{align*} Block \(j\) contributes the \(j\)-th derivative of \(\textrm{\runic ᛉ}\); for \(k = 1\) this is step 3 of Appendix B.14.

  3. Integrate by parts, \(j\) times for block \(j\). The functions \(\lambda \mapsto (\partial_{jd+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k)}_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \big)\) are smooth (\(\mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}\) and \(\gamma\) are smooth). Inserting step 3 into step 2, the derivative of the action is a sum over the blocks, \[ \frac{d}{d\textrm{\runic ᛊ}} S_{[a,b]}[\gamma_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ}}] \Big|_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ} = 0} = \int_a^b \sum_{j=0}^{k} \sum_{m=1}^d (\partial_{jd+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} \, ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k)}_\mathcal{U} \big) \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(j)m} \, d\lambda , \] and in the term of block \(j\) the deformation enters through its \(j\)-th derivative. One integration by parts moves one derivative from \(\textrm{\runic ᛉ}\) onto the derivative of the Lagrangian: \begin{align*} &\int_a^b (\partial_{jd+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} \, ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k)}_\mathcal{U} \big) \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(j)m} \, d\lambda \\ \xlongrightarrow{\text{product rule}} \; &\int_a^b \frac{d}{d\lambda} \Big[ (\partial_{jd+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} \, ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k)}_\mathcal{U} \big) \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(j-1)m} \Big] d\lambda \\ &\qquad - \int_a^b \frac{d}{d\lambda} \Big[ (\partial_{jd+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} \, ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k)}_\mathcal{U} \big) \Big] \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(j-1)m} \, d\lambda \\ \xlongrightarrow{\text{fund.\ theorem of calculus}} \; &\Big[ (\partial_{jd+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} \, ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k)}_\mathcal{U} \big) \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(j-1)m} \Big]_a^b \\ &\qquad - \int_a^b \frac{d}{d\lambda} \Big[ (\partial_{jd+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} \, ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k)}_\mathcal{U} \big) \Big] \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(j-1)m} \, d\lambda \\ \xlongrightarrow{\textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(j-1)}(a) \, = \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(j-1)}(b) \, = \, 0} \; &- \int_a^b \frac{d}{d\lambda} \Big[ (\partial_{jd+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} \, ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k)}_\mathcal{U} \big) \Big] \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(j-1)m} \, d\lambda . \end{align*} The result has the same form, with one more derivative on the first factor, one less on \(\textrm{\runic ᛉ}\), and a factor \(-1\). Repeating the same three moves, each time using one more of the conditions \(\textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(j-2)} = \dots = \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(0)} = 0\) at \(a\) and \(b\), after \(j\) integrations by parts \[ \int_a^b (\partial_{jd+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} \, ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k)}_\mathcal{U} \big) \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(j)m} \, d\lambda = (-1)^j \int_a^b \frac{d^j}{d\lambda^j} \Big[ (\partial_{jd+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} \, ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k)}_\mathcal{U} \big) \Big] \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^m \, d\lambda . \] Block \(j\) uses the conditions on \(\textrm{\runic ᛉ}, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}', \dots, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(j-1)}\), and the highest block, \(j = k\), uses all of them: this is why \(k - 1\) derivatives of \(\textrm{\runic ᛉ}\) must vanish at the endpoints. Doing this for every block, and collecting the factor \(\textrm{\runic ᛉ}^m\), \[ \frac{d}{d\textrm{\runic ᛊ}} S_{[a,b]}[\gamma_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ}}] \Big|_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ} = 0} = \int_a^b \sum_{m=1}^d \left\{ \sum_{j=0}^{k} (-1)^j \frac{d^j}{d\lambda^j} \Big[ (\partial_{jd+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} \, ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k)}_\mathcal{U} \big) \Big] \right\} \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^m(\lambda) \, d\lambda . \] For \(k = 1\) this is step 4 of Appendix B.14: block \(0\) needs no integration by parts, block \(1\) needs one.

  4. From the integral to every point. As in Appendix B.14, with the sum over \(j\) in the integrand of step 4 in place of the bracket there. Suppose, on the contrary, that \(\gamma\) is a critical curve but this sum is non-zero for some \(m\) at some \(\lambda_0 \in (a,b)\), and choose the sum itself as the variation: \[ \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^m(\lambda) \coloneqq \big( (\lambda - a)(b - \lambda) \big)^k \sum_{j=0}^{k} (-1)^j \frac{d^j}{d\lambda^j} \Big[ (\partial_{jd+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} \, ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k)}_\mathcal{U} \big) \Big] . \] The only new point is admissibility, which now also requires \(\textrm{\runic ᛉ}', \dots, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(k-1)}\) to vanish at the endpoints. This is why the prefactor is raised to the power \(k\): it vanishes to order \(k\) at \(a\) and \(b\), so its first \(k-1\) derivatives vanish there too. By the Leibniz rule, every derivative \(\textrm{\runic ᛉ}^{(i)m}\) with \(i \leq k-1\) is a sum of terms, each containing a derivative of order at most \(k - 1\) of the prefactor, and therefore vanishes at \(a\) and \(b\). The rest is as there: the integrand of step 4 is the non-negative prefactor times the sum over \(m\) of the squares of these sums, positive near \(\lambda_0\), so the derivative of the action is positive, a contradiction. \(\square\)

Remarks.

  1. Order of the equations and boundary data. If \(\mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}\) genuinely depends on the last block, the term \(j = k\) of the Statement differentiates \(k\) more times a function of \(\gamma^{(k)}_\mathcal{U}\), so the equations contain \(\gamma^{(2k)}_\mathcal{U}\): a system of \(d\) ordinary differential equations of order \(2k\). Such a system needs \(2k\) pieces of data per component, which is exactly what the variations keep fixed: \(\gamma_\mathcal{U}, \dots, \gamma^{(k-1)}_\mathcal{U}\) at \(a\), and the same at \(b\). For \(k = 1\): second-order equations, and fixed endpoints.

  2. Total derivatives. Let \(K\) be a smooth function of the first \(k\) blocks only, \(K\big( \alpha_{(0)} ; \dots ; \alpha_{(k-1)} \big)\). Along a curve, by the chain rule, \[ \frac{d}{d\lambda} \Big[ K\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k-1)}_\mathcal{U} \big) \Big] = \sum_{j=0}^{k-1} \sum_{m=1}^d (\partial_{jd+m} K)\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k-1)}_\mathcal{U} \big) \, \gamma^{(j+1)m}_\mathcal{U} , \] the evaluation on the curve of a Lagrangian of order \(k\), linear in the last block. Its action is \(K\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U}(b) ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k-1)}_\mathcal{U}(b) \big) - K\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U}(a) ; \dots ; \gamma^{(k-1)}_\mathcal{U}(a) \big)\), by the fundamental theorem of calculus, and it is the same for all varied curves, since they share these data with \(\gamma\). Its derivative w.r.t. \(\textrm{\runic ᛊ}\) thus vanishes for every \(\textrm{\runic ᛉ}\) and every curve, so, by the Statement, its Euler–Lagrange expression vanishes identically. Adding it to any Lagrangian leaves the equations unchanged. For \(k = 2\) this can be checked directly: with \(\tilde{\mathcal{L}}_\mathscr{X}(\alpha_{(0)} ; \alpha_{(1)} ; \alpha_{(2)}) = (\partial_i K) \, \alpha^i_{(1)} + (\partial_{d+i} K) \, \alpha^i_{(2)}\), on the curve \[ \partial_m \tilde{\mathcal{L}}_\mathscr{X} = \frac{d}{d\lambda} \big[ \partial_m K \big], \qquad \partial_{d+m} \tilde{\mathcal{L}}_\mathscr{X} = \partial_m K + \frac{d}{d\lambda} \big[ \partial_{d+m} K \big], \qquad \partial_{2d+m} \tilde{\mathcal{L}}_\mathscr{X} = \partial_{d+m} K , \] and the alternating sum of the Statement gives \(\frac{d}{d\lambda} [\partial_m K] - \frac{d}{d\lambda} [\partial_m K] - \frac{d^2}{d\lambda^2} [\partial_{d+m} K] + \frac{d^2}{d\lambda^2} [\partial_{d+m} K] = 0\). This is how second derivatives can sit in a Lagrangian without raising the order of its equations: a first-order Lagrangian plus \(\frac{d}{d\lambda} K(\gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U})\) contains \(\ddot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}\), linearly, and still has second-order equations. The Lagrangian of General Relativity is of this kind: its second derivatives of the metric components can be collected into a total derivative, which is why the Einstein equations are of second order (the remainder, quadratic in first derivatives, is then no longer chart independent).
